verses.1: Rise, Mighty One, who liest in the waters, and enter this thy fair and glorious kingdom. Let Rohita who made this All uphold thee carefully nurtured for supreme dominion.
verses.2: The strength that was in waters hath ascended. Mount o'er the tribes which thou hast generated. Creating Soma, waters, plants and cattle, bring hitherward both quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.3: Ye Maruts, strong and mighty, sons of Prisni, with Indra for ally crush down our foemen. Let Rohita, ye bounteous givers, hear you, thrice-seven Maruts who delight in sweetness!
verses.4: Up to the lap of births, to lofty places, hath Rohita, the germ of Dames, ascended. Conjoined with these he found the six realms: seeing his way in front here he received the kingship.
verses.5: For thee hath Rohita obtained dominion, scattered thine enemies, become thy safeguard. So by the potent Sakvaris let Heaven and Earth be milked toyield thee all thy wishes.
verses.6: Rohita gave the Earth and Heavens their being. There Parameshthin held the cord extended. Thereon reposeth Aja Ekapada. He with his might hath stablished Earth and Heaven.
verses.7: Rohita firmly stablished Earth and Heaven: by him was ether fixt by him the welkin. He measured out mid air and all the regions: by him the Gods found life that lasts for ever.
verses.8: Arranging shoots, springs, Rohita considered this Universe in all its forms and phases. May he, gone up to heaven with mighty glory, anoint thy sovranty with milk and fatness.
verses.9: Thy risings up, thy mountings and ascensions wherewith thou fillest heaven and air's mid-region-- By prayer for these, by milk of these, increasing, in Rohita's kingdom watch, among his people.
verses.10: The tribes thy heat produced have followed hither the Calf and Gayatri, the strain that lauds him. With friendly heart let them approach to serve thee, and the Calf Rohita come with his mother.
verses.11: Erected, Rohita hath reached the welkin, wise, young, creating every form and figure. Agni, refulgent with his heightened lustre, in the third realm hath brought us joy and gladness.
verses.12: Thousand-horned Bull, may Jatavedas, worshipped with butter, balmed with Soma, rich in heroes, Besought, ne'er quit me; may I ne'er forsake thee. Give me abundant men and herds of cattle.
verses.13: Rohita is the sire and mouth of worship: to him with voice, ear, heart I pay oblation. To Rohita come Gods with joyful spirit. May he by risings raise me till I join him.
verses.14: Rohita ordered sacrifice for Visvakarman: thence have I obtained this strength and energy. May I proclaim thee as my kin over the greatness of the world.
verses.15: On thee have mounted Brihati and Pankti. and Kakup with great splendour, Jatavedas! The cry of Vashat with the voice uplifted and Rohita with seed on thee have mounted.
verses.16: He goes into the womb of earth, he robes himself in heaven and air. He on the Bright One's station hath reached heavenly light and all the worlds.
verses.17: To us, Vachaspati, may Earth be pleasant, pleasant our dwelling, pleasant be our couches. Even here may Prana be our friend: may Agni, O Parameshthin give thee life and splendour.
verses.18: And those, Vachaspati, our own five seasons, sacred to Visvakarman their creator. Even here our friend be Prana: Parameshthin, may Rohita vouchsafe the life and splendour.
verses.19: Breed, O Vachaspati, joy and understanding, kine i n our stall and children in our consorts. Even here may Prana be our friend: may Agni, O Parameshthin, give thee life and splendour.
verses.20: With splendour let God Savitar, and Agni, with splendour Mitra, Varuna invest thee. Treading down all Malignities, come hither. Pleasant and' glorious hast thou made this kingdom.
verses.21: Rohita, car-borne by a speckled leader, thou, pouring water,. goest on in triumph.
verses.22: Golden, refulgent, lofty is the Lady, Rohini, Rohita's devoted Consort. Through her may we win various spoil and booty, through her be conquerors in every battle.
verses.23: Rohita's seat is Rohini before us: that is the path the speckled Mare pursueth. Kasyapas and Gandharvas lead her upward, and heavenly sages ever watch and guard her,
verses.24: Surya's bay steeds refulgent and immortal draw the light-rolling. chariot on for ever. Drinker of fatness, Rohita, resplendent, hath entered into various-coloured heaven,
verses.25: Rohita, Bull whose horns are sharply pointed, superior of Agni and of Surya, He who supports the sundered earth and heaven,--from him the Gods effect their own creations.
verses.26: Rohita rose to heaven from mighty ocean, Rohita rose and clomb all steeps and rises.
verses.27: Prepare the Milky One who teems with fatness: she is the Gods' never-reluctant milch-cow. Indra drink Soma: ours be peace and safety. Let Agni lead the laud, and chase our foemen.
verses.28: Both kindling and inflamed, adored with butter and enhanced thereby. May conquering Agni, conqueror of all, destroy mine enemies.
verses.29: Let him smite down in death and burn the foeman who attacketh me. Our adversaries we consume through Agni the Carnivorous.
verses.30: Beat them down, Indra, with thy bolt, beat them down, mighty with thine arm. I through the energy and force of Agni have secured my foes.
verses.31: Cast down our foes beneath our feet, O Agni. Brihaspati, oppress our rebel kinsman. Low let them fall, O Indra-Agni. Mitra-Varuna, powerless to show their anger.
verses.32: Ascending up on high, O God. O Surya, drive my foes away. Yea, beat them backward with the stone: to deepest darkness let them go.
verses.33: Calf of Viraj, the Bull of prayers and worship, whitebacked, he hath gone up to air's mid-region. Singing, they hymn the Calf, with gifts of butter: him who is Brahma they exalt with Brahma.
verses.34: Rise up to earth, rise up to heaven above it; rise up to opulence, rise up to kingship. Rise up to offspring, rise to life immortal; rise, and with Rohita unite thy body.
verses.35: With all the Gods who circle round the Sun, upholding royal sway, With all of these may Rohita accordant, give sovranty to thee with friendly spirit.
verses.36: Cleansed by prayer, sacrifices bear thee upward: bay coursers, ever travelling, convey thee. Thy light shines over sea and billowy ocean.
verses.37: Rohita, conqueror of cows and riches and gathered spoil, is heaven's and earth's upholder. Over earth's greatness would I tell my kinship with thee who hast a thousand births and seven.
verses.38: A glorious sight to beasts and men, thou goest glorious to the regions and mid-regions. On earth's, on Aditi's bosom, bright with glory. Fain would I equal Savitar in beauty.
verses.39: Thou, yonder, knowest all things here, when here thou knowest what is there. From here men see the sphere of light, Surya profoundly wise in heaven.
verses.40: A God, thou injurest the Gods: thou movest in the ocean's depth. Men kindle common Agni: him only the higher sages know.
verses.41: Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her Calf at foot, the Cow hath risen Whitherward, to what place hath she departed? Where doth she calve? Not in this herd of cattle.
verses.42: She hath become one-footed or two-footed, four-footed, or eight-footed or nine-footed, This universe's thousand-syllabled Pankti Oceans flow forth from her in all directions.
verses.43: Rising to heaven, immortal, hear my calling. Cleansed by prayer, sacrifices bear thee upward. Bay coursers, ever on the road, convey thee.
verses.44: This, O Immortal One, I know of thee, thy progress to the sky thy dwelling-place in loftiest heaven.
verses.45: Beyond the sky, beyond the Earth looks Surya, and beyond the floods. The single eye of all that is; to mighty heaven hath he arisen.
verses.46: The earth was made his altar, and the wide expanses were the fence. There Rohita established both these Agnis, fervent heat and cold.
verses.47: He stablished heat and cold, he made the mountains sacrificial posts. Then both the Agnis, Rohita's who found celestial light, with rain for molten butter, sacrificed.
verses.48: Rohita's Agni-his who found heaven's light-is kindled with the prayer. From him the heat, from him the cold, from him the sacrifice was born.
verses.49: Both Agins-Rohita's who found the light of heaven--made strong by prayer, Waxing by prayer, adored with prayer, by prayer enkindled, sacrificed.
verses.50: One is deposited in Truth, one kindled in the waters: both Agnis of Rohita who found the light are set aflame with prayer.
verses.51: That decked by Wind, and that prepared by Indra Brahmanaspati, Agnis of Rohita who found light, prayer-enkindled, sacrificed.
verses.52: Rohita made the earth to be his altar, heaven his Dakshina. Then heat he took for Agni, and with rain for molten butter he created every living thing.
verses.53: The earth became an altar, heat was Agni, and the butter rain. There Agni made, by song and hymn, these mountains rise and stand erect.
verses.54: Then, having made the hills stand up, Rohita spake to Earth, and said: In thee let every thing be born, what is and what is yet to be.
verses.55: This sacrifice, the first of all, the past, the present, had its birth. From that arose this universe, yea, all this world of brightness, brought by Rohita the heavenly Sage.
verses.56: If thou should kick a cow, or by indecent act offend the Sun, Thy root I sever; nevermore mayst thou cast shadow on the ground.
verses.57: Thou who, between the fire and me, passest across the line of shade. Thy root I sever: nevermore mayst thou cast shadow on the ground.
verses.58: Whoe'er he be who, Surya, God! comes between thee and me to-day, On him we wipe away ill-dream, and troubles, and impurity.
verses.59: Let us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser's sacrifice. Let not malignities dwell with us.
verses.60: May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out tc reach the Gods, That perfecteth our sacrifice.
verses.61: Radiant, refulgent in the sky are reared the banners of his light, Aditya's, who beholdeth man, mighty in act and bountiful.
verses.62: Let us laud him, the whole world's Herdsman, Surya, who with his rays illumines all the regions, Mark of the quarters, brightening them with lustre, swift, mighty-pinioned, flying in the ocean.
verses.63: From west to east thou speedest freely, making by magic day and night of diverse colours. This is Aditya, thy transcendent glory, that thou alone art born through all creation.
verses.64: Victorious, inspired, and brightly shining, whom seven strong tawny-coloured coursers carry, Whom Atri lifted from the flood to heaven, thus men behold thee as thy course thou runnest.
verses.65: Let them not snare thee speeding on thy journey: pass safely, swiftly places hard to traverse, While measuring out the day and night thou movest--O Surya, even Heaven and Earth the Goddess.
verses.66: Hail to thy rapid car whereon, O Surya, thou circlest in a moment both the limits, Whirled by thy bay steeds, best of all at drawing, thy hundred horses or seven goodly coursers!
verses.67: Mount thy strong car, O Surya, lightly rolling, drawn by good steeds, propitious, brightly gleaming, Whirled by thy bays, most excellent at drawing, thy hundred horses or seven goodly coursers.
verses.68: Surya hath harnessed to his car to draw him seven stately bay steeds gay with wolden housings. The Bright One started from the distant region: dispelling gloom the God hath climbed the heavens.
verses.69: With lofty banner hath the God gone upward, and introduced the light, expelling darkness. He hath looked round on all the worlds, the Hero, the son of Aditi, Celestial Eagle.
verses.70: Rising, thou spreadest out thy rays, thou nourishest all shapes and forms. Thou with thy power illumest both the oceans, encompassing all spheres with thy refulgence.
verses.71: Moving by magic power to east and westward, these two young creatures, sporting, circle ocean. One of the pair beholds all living creatures: with wheels of gold the bay steeds bear the other.
verses.72: Atri established thee in heaven. O Surya, to create the month. So on thou goest, firmly held, heating, beholding all that is.
verses.73: As the Calf both his parents so thou joinest both the distant bounds, Surely the Gods up yonder knew this sacred mystery long ago.
verses.74: Surya is eager to obtain all wealth that lies along the sea, Great is the course spread out for him, his eastward and his westward path.
verses.75: He finishes his race with speed and never turns his thought aside, Thereby he keeps not from the Gods enjoyment of the Drink of Life.
verses.76: His heralds bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that live, Surya, that all may look on him.
verses.77: The Constellations pass away, like thieves, departing in the night. Before the all-beholding Sun.
verses.78: His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o'er the world of men, Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
verses.79: Swift and all-beautiful art thou, O Surya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
verses.80: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind, Hither, all light to behold.
verses.81: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou seest, brilliant Varuna. The active one among mankind,
verses.82: Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days, Sun, seeing all things that have life.
verses.83: Seven bay steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One, God, Surya, with the radiant hair.
verses.84: Surya, hath yoked the pure bright seven, the daughters of the car, with these, His own dear team, he travelleth.
verses.85: Devout, aflame with fervent heat, Rohita hath gone up to heaven. He is re-born, returning to his birthplace, and hath become the Gods' imperial ruler.
verses.86: Dear unto all men, facing all directions, with hands and palms on every side extended, He, the sole God, engendering earth and heaven, beareth them with his wings and arms together.
verses.87: The single-footed hath outstepped the biped, the biped overtakes the triple-footed. The biped hath outstridden the six-footed: these sit around the single-footed's body.
verses.88: When he, unwearied, fain to go, hath mounted his bays, he makes two colours, brightly shining. Rising with banners, conquering the regions, thou sendest light through all the floods, Aditya.
verses.89: Verily, Surya, thou art great: truly, Aditya, thou art great. Great is thy grandeur, Mighty One: thou, O Aditya, thou art great.
verses.90: In heaven, O Bird, and in mid-air thou shinest: thou shinest on the earth and in the waters. Thou hast pervaded both the seas with splendour: a God art thou, O God, light-winner, mighty.
verses.91: Soaring in mid-course hither from the distance, fleet and inspired, the Bird that flies above us, With might advancing Vishnu manifested, he conquers all that moves with radiant banner:
verses.92: Brilliant, observant, mighty Lord, an Eagle illuming both the spheres and air between them. Day and the Night, clad in the robes of Surya, spread forth more widely all his hero powers.
verses.93: Flaming and radiant, strengthening his body, bestowing floods that promptly come to meet us, He, luminous, winged, mighty, strength-bestower, hath mounted all the regions as he forms them.
verses.94: Bright presence of the Gods, the luminous herald Surya hath mounted the celestial regions. Day's maker, he hath shone away the darkness, and radiant, passed o'er places hard to traverse.
verses.95: He hath gone up on high, the Gods' bright presence, the eye of Mitra, Varuna and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, Surya hath filled the earth and air and heaven,
verses.96: High in the midst of heaven may we behold thee whom men call Savitar, the bright red Eagle, Soaring and speeding on thy way, refulgent, unwasting light which Atri erst discovered.
verses.97: Him, Son of Aditi, an Eagle hasting along heaven's height, I supplicate in terror, As such prolong our lengthened life, O Surya: may we, unharmed, enjoy thy gracious favour.
verses.98: This gold-hued Hansa's wings, soaring to heaven, spread o'er a thousand days' continued journey Supporting all the Gods upon his bosom, he goes his way beholding every creature.
verses.99: Rohita, in primeval days Prajapati, was, after, Time, Mouth of all sacrifices, he, Rohita, brought celestial light.
verses.100: He, Rohita, became the world: Rohita gave the heaven its heat. Rohita with his beams of light travelled along the earth and sea.
verses.101: To all the regions Rohita came, the imperial Lord of heaven. He watches over ocean, heaven, and earth and all existing things.
verses.102: Mounting the lofty ones, he, bright, unwearied, splendidly shining, makes two separate colours, While through all worlds that are he sends his lustre, radiant, observant, mighty, wind-approacher.
verses.103: One form comes on, the other is reverted: to day and night the Strong One shapes and fits him. With humble prayer for aid we call on Surya, who knows the way, whose home is in the region.
verses.104: The suppliant's way, filling the earth, the Mighty circleth the world with eye that none deceiveth. May he, all-seeing, well-disposed and holy, give ear and listen to the word I utter.
verses.105: Blazing with light his majesty hath compassed ocean and earth and heaven and air's mid-region. May he, all-seeing, well-disposed and holy, give ear and listen to the word I utter.
verses.106: Agni is weakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow, Like young trees shooting up on high their branches, his flames are mounting to the vault of heaven.
verses.107: He who engendered these, the earth and heaven, who made the worlds the mantle that he weareth, In whom abide the six wide-spreading regions through which the Bird's keen vision penetrateth, This God is wroth offended by the sinner who wrongs the Brahman who hath gained this knowledge Agitate him, O Rohita; destroy him: entangle in thy snares the Braman's tyrant.
verses.108: He from whom winds blow pure in ordered season, from whom the seas flow forth in all directions, This God, etc.
verses.109: He who takes life away, he who bestows it; from whom comes breath to every living creature, This God, etc.
verses.110: Who with the breath he draws sates earth and heaven, with expiration fills the ocean's belly, This God, etc.
verses.111: In whom Viraj, Prajapati, Parameshthin, Agni Vaisvanara abide with Pankti, He who hath taken to himself the breathing of the Supreme, the vigour of the Highest, This God, etc.
verses.112: On whom rest six expenses and five regions, four waters, and three syllables of worship, He who hath looked between both spheres in anger, This God, etc.
verses.113: He who, consuming food, became its master, the Lord of Prayer, the Regent of Devotion, The world's Lord, present and to be hereafter, This God, etc.
verses.114: He who metes out the thirteenth month, constructed with days and nights, containing thirty members, This God, etc.
verses.115: Dark the descent; the strong-winged birds are golden: they fly aloft to heaven, enrobed in waters. They have come hither from the seat of Order, This God, etc.
verses.116: What silver. Kasyapa, thou hast refulgent, what brightly-shining lotus-flower collected, Wherein are gathered seven Suns together, This God, etc.
verses.117: In front the Brihat-Saman is his mantle, and from behind Rathantara enfolds him, Ever with care robing themselves in splendour. This God, etc.
verses.118: One of his wings was Brihat, and the other Rathantarr., vigorous with one same purpose, What time the Gods gave Rohita his being. This God, etc.
verses.119: At evening he is Varuna and Agni, ascending in the morning he is Mitra. As Savitar, he moves through air's mid region, as Indra warmsthe heavens from the centre. This God, etc.
verses.120: This gold-hued Harisa's wings, soaring to heaven spread o'er a thousand days' continued journey. Supporting all the Gods upon his bosom, he goes his way beholding every creature. This God, etc.
verses.121: This is the God who dwells-within the waters, the thousandrooted, many-powered Atri, He who brought all this world into existence. This God; etc.
verses.122: With flying feet his tawny coursers carry the bright God through, the sky, aglow with splendour. Whose limbs uplifted fire and heat the heavens: hither he shineswith beams of golden colour. This God, etc.
verses.123: He beside whom his bay steeds bear the Adityas, by whom as sacrifice go many knowing. The sole light shining spread through various places. This God, etc.
verses.124: This seven make the one-wheeled chariot ready: bearing seven names the single courser draws it. The wheel, three-naved, is sound and undecaying: thereon these worlds of life are all dependent. This God, etc.
verses.125: Eight times attached the potent Courser draws it, Sire of the Gods, father of hymns and praises. So Matarisvan, measuring in spirit the thread of Order, purifies all regions. This God, etc.
verses.126: The thread that goes through all celestial quarters within the Gayatri, womb of life eternal. This God, etc.
verses.127: There are the settings, three the upward risings, three are thespaces, yea, and three the heavens. We know thy triple place of birth, O Agni, we know the deities'' triple generations.
verses.128: He who, as soon as born, laid broad earth open, and set the ocean in the air's mid-region, This God, etc.
verses.129: Thou, Agni, kind with lights and mental powers, hast up in heaven shone as the Sun, enkindled. The Maruts, sons of Prisni, sang his praises what time the Gods gave Rohita his being. This God, etc.
verses.130: Giver of breath, giver of strength and vigour, he whose commandment all the Gods acknowledge, He who is Lord of this, of man and cattle, This God, etc.
verses.131: The single-footed hath outstepped the biped, the biped overtakes the triple-footed. The quadruped hath wrought when bipeds called him, standing and looking on the five collected. This God is wroth offended by the sinner that wrongs the Brahman who hath gained this knowledge. Agitate him, O Rohita; destroy him: entangle in thy snares the Brahman's tyrant.
verses.132: Born is the darksome Mother's Son, the whitely shining Calf of Night. He, Rohita, ascendeth up to heaven, hath mounted to the heights.
verses.133: Down looking, on the ridge of sky Savitar goes to highest heaven.
verses.134: To misty cloud filled with his rays Mahendra goes encompassed round.
verses.135: Creator and Ordainer, he is Vayu, he is lifted cloud.
verses.136: Rudra, and Mahadeva, he is Aryaman and Varuna.
verses.137: Agni is he, and Siirya, he is verily Mahayama.
verses.138: Calves, joined, stand close beside him, ten in number, with one single head.
verses.139: From west to east they bend their way: when he mounts up he shines afar.
verses.140: His are these banded Maruts: they move gathered close like porters' thongs.
verses.141: To misty cloud filled with his rays Mahendra goes encompassed round,
verses.142: His are the nine supports, the casks set in nine several places here.
verses.143: He keeppeth watch o'er creatures, all that breatheth and that breatheth not.
verses.144: This conquering might hath entered him, He is the sole the simple One, the One alone.
verses.145: In him these Deities become simple and One
verses.146: Both fame and glory and water (? ámbhas) and cloud-mass and Brahman-splendor and food and food-eating.
verses.147: He who knows this single god—
verses.148: Not second, not third, also not fourth is he called.
verses.149: Not fifth, not sixth, also not seventh is he called.
verses.150: Not eighth, not ninth, also not tenth is he called.
verses.151: He looks abroad for everything, both what breathes and what does not.
verses.152: Into him is entered this power; he himself is one, single, one only.
verses.153: All the gods in him become single.
verses.154: Both worship (bráhman) and penance and fame and glory and water and cloud-mass and Brahman-splendor and food and food-eating—
verses.155: And what is and what shall be and faith and sheen and heaven (svargá) and svadhā́.
verses.156: He who knows this single god—
verses.157: He verily [is] death, he immortality (amṛ́ta), he the monster (abhvà), he the demon.
verses.158: He [is] Rudra, winner of good, in the giving of good; in the expression of homage, [he is] the utterance váṣaṭ, put together after.
verses.159: All these familiar demons (yātú) wait upon his direction (praśís).
verses.160: In his control are all yon asterisms, together with the moon.
verses.161: He verily was born of the day; of him the day was born.
verses.162: He verily was born of the night; of him the night was born.
verses.163: He verily was born of the atmosphere; of him the atmosphere was born.
verses.164: He verily was born of Vāyu (wind); of him Vāyu was born.
verses.165: He verily was born of the sky; out of him the sky was born.
verses.166: He verily was born of the quarters; of him the quarters were born.
verses.167: He verily was born of the earth; of him the earth was born.
verses.168: He verily was born of fire; of him fire was born.
verses.169: He verily was born of the waters; of him the waters were born.
verses.170: He verily was born of the verses (ṛ́c); of him the verses were born.
verses.171: He verily was born of the sacrifice; of him the sacrifice was born.
verses.172: He is the sacrifice; his is the sacrifice; he [is] made the head of the sacrifice.
verses.173: He thunders; he lightens; he indeed hurls the stone.
verses.174: Either for the evil [man] or for the excellent; for man or for Asura.
verses.175: Either when thou makest the herbs, or when thou rainest excellently, or when thou hast increased him of the people (? janyá).
verses.176: Such, O bountiful one, is thy greatness; and thine, too (úpa), are a hundred bodies.
verses.177: Thine, too, are two billions, [many] billions (?); or else thou art a hundred million.
verses.178: More is Indra than non-dying (??); more art thou, O Indra, than the deaths.
verses.179: More than the niggard, lord of strength (śácī) art thou, O Indra; as called mighty, prevailing, do we worship (upa-ās) thee.
verses.180: Homage be to thee, O conspicuous one (paśyata); see páśya me, O conspicuous one.
verses.181: With food-eating, with glory, with brilliancy (téjas), with Brahman-splendor;
verses.182: As called water (? ámbhas), force (áma), greatness, power, do we worship thee.
verses.183: As called water (ámbhas), red, silvery (rajatá), welkin (rájas), power, do we worship thee.
verses.184: As called wide, broad, happy (subhū́), earths (? bhúvas), do we worship thee.
verses.185: As called breadth, width, expanse, world, do we worship thee.
verses.186: As called one of arising good, of increasing (??) good, of gathering good, of coming good, do we worship thee.
verses.187: Homage be to thee, O conspicuous one; see me, O conspicuous one.
verses.188: With food-eating, with glory, with brilliancy, with Brahman-splendor.
